desc:
Consider every substring t of s that satisfies both rules:

  • its length is between minSize and maxSize inclusive;
  • it contains at most maxLetters different letters.

Return the largest number of times any such t occurs in s. Occurrences may overlap. If no substring satisfies the rules, return 0.

s = "aababcaab", maxLetters = 2, minSize = 3, maxSize = 4
"aab" is allowed and occurs at positions 0 and 6
result = 2
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Brute force over all lengths from minSize to maxSize and all start positions is too much work for 8,000 characters and 26 lengths... but is every length really needed?
If a substring of length L > minSize occurs c times, then its first minSize characters occur at least c times too, and still satisfy the letter limit.
So only length minSize matters. Slide a window of that length, maintain the number of distinct letters, and count the allowed windows in a hash map.
editorial: Take any valid substring t longer than minSize with c occurrences. Its prefix of length minSize occurs at every one of those places, so at least c times; it has no more distinct letters than t, and has a legal length. Therefore the best answer is always achieved at length exactly minSize, and maxSize never changes the result (it is only a distraction).

Slide a window of length minSize and keep letter counts to know the number of distinct letters in O(1) per step. Whenever the window has at most maxLetters distinct letters, increment its count in a hash map keyed by the substring text (at most 26 characters). The answer is the largest value in the map, or 0. Time O(n · minSize) for hashing the slices, i.e. O(n) for these limits.
